investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-08-17 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the remote agent pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner received zero evidence — all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by node affinity or selector rules and cannot be used even via preemption. As a result, every remote-agent pod request is immediately Unschedulable, the agent VM is never created, and the eval contract cannot be satisfied. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is currently confirmed only at the eval layer.

The snapshot's source field reports "desktop-nightly-release" rather than "github-actions", indicating the scheduled GitHub Actions workflow that is expected to publish a fresh snapshot either did not run, failed silently, or did not push an updated file to the GitHub Pages branch in time. The result is a stale artifact that violates the snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 assertion defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482.
